note: THE CASE THAT SEPARATES `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'` FROM `String.toLowerCase()`. `tr` in the C locale maps A-Z ONLY, so U+0130 (Latin capital I with dot above) reaches the `[^a-z0-9]+` pass intact and is eaten as punctuation: `İstanbul gap` normalizes to `stanbul gap` and matches an older `stanbul gap`. JavaScript's toLowerCase() expands that character to `i` plus a combining dot, so a port using it would key on `i stanbul gap`, find NO duplicate, and leave two open issues for the same gap.
